design_critique: 1) Attribution is broken. The raced baseline (iteration 0, 39.85 score) used sensor y=0.06, sensor_size=0.016, kp=5, kd=0.02, base 1.7, ki=0. The revised design moves sensors back to y=0.04 and shrinks sensor_size to 0.012, and it also changes kp to 4, kd to 0.1, base to 1.6 and ki to 0. The rationale calls geometry 'unchanged from the authorized baseline', but it is unchanged only from the input file, not from the design that produced the 60 trials. A next-race result therefore cannot be attributed to any single controller change, despite the stated goal of clean attribution. 2) Sensor placement moves the wrong way for the failure mode. The evidence is early drift with 2 line losses per run. Shortening lookahead from 0.06 m to 0.04 m reduces the time the controller has to react to a bend, and the rationale never justifies this. The 0.012 footprint also leaves 3 mm gaps between sensors at 15 mm spacing, so a tape edge can fall between sensors. The rationale's own reasoning in the draft favoured the forward, overlapping layout. 3) Lowering kp from 5 to 4 reduces steering authority on sharp bends, which is where the 2 line losses per run most plausibly occur. The rationale's overshoot explanation is not supported by the data: steering_oscillation (0.16 to 0.18) and max_error (about 0.06) do not separate overshoot from late turning. A lower kp may simply worsen understeer on the s-bend and slalom. 4) kd=0.1 is five times the raced value of 0.02. The arithmetic is right (about 100*kd*d turn units per step, so 0.02 per step gives 0.2 units), but the rationale does not show that jitter at the new geometry, with smaller footprints and partial-cover readings, stays below this. The noise-to-turn comparison is made only against the 0.01 to 0.03 noise figure, which is a guess. 5) Speed: base 1.6 is a 6 percent cut, but the only completion evidence is that 1.5 m/s average is needed and the base-to-m/s map is unmeasured. The cut may not make completion more likely, since progress was 0.06 to 0.17 at base 1.7 and the failure is off-track, not time. 6) The off-track threshold in the expectations is wrong. The rule is max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4) = 0.06 m, so max_error below 0.06 is only the failure boundary, not a safety margin. A pass at 0.06 would still be a fail.
rationale_critique: 1) The rationale says kd 0.3 to 0.1 keeps damping 'at about 10 units', and it rejects 0.6 as mis-scaled. That is internally consistent, but it then argues that kd=0.02 was too small to matter without any evidence on which side of the trade-off the raced design sits. 2) The saturation argument is restated as steering loss. Outer-wheel saturation near |signal| 0.6 only limits outer-wheel speed-up; the inner wheel still slows, so authority is reduced, not lost. The rationale does not acknowledge this correction from round 1. 3) The integral removal is justified only by the clamp magnitude (0.1 turn units). It does not address the round-1 point that the 2 percent left/right motor mismatch causes a steady offset of roughly mismatch/kp, which matters more when kp is lowered. 4) The rationale calls base 1.6 a 'compromise' without a number for completion-time margin. At 1.6 the time term falls and completion risk may rise, and the rationale gives no fallback if the first race fails to complete. 5) The falsifiable expectations are useful, but several are weak. 'Steering_oscillation below the 0.16 to 0.18 baseline' is a weak test because the change set gives no mechanism to reduce it strongly. 'max_error below 0.06' sits on the failure boundary, as noted above. 6) The rationale does not state which single change to revert first if the next race fails, which the attribution goal requires. The falsifiable tests name conditions for kd and kp but do not state which of the four controller changes, or the geometry change, to undo first.
